Subject: Question on cache billing: when are prefix hits charged?

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — Acme's engineering and procurement teams are reviewing the draft rate card you shared. One outstanding question from finance: for our conversational search workload (large cohort of identical system prompts + user queries), how does Redwood bill when the "prefix" or prompt cache returns a stored response? Specifically:

- If the system prompt + user prefix exactly matches a cached entry and Redwood returns the cached continuation, do we get charged input tokens, output tokens, both, or neither?
- Is there a separate cache-read fee or is it covered by the per-token rate?
- We have some warm-prefetching (precomputing responses for common prefixes). Is prefetch generation considered billable compute when it happens?

We want to model monthly costs and would prefer a clear rule we can embed into our cost calculator. Can you confirm? Attaching our sample traffic scenarios (cache-scenarios.xlsx).

Best,
Alice

Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Question on cache billing: when are prefix hits charged?

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the spreadsheet, that helps. Short answer up front to help your finance team: when a prefix/prompt cache results in an exact match and the cached response is returned without re-running the model, Acme will not be billed for the model compute tokens that the cached segment represents. You will still be billed for any newly generated tokens (the continuation after the cached span).

A few additional points:
- Input tokens that are only used to look up the cache (i.e., the prompt/prefix you sent) are not billed if the cache returns a fully satisfied cached response. If the system must re-run the model (partial hit or fallback), standard input+output token billing applies.
- We surface a small per-request cache retrieval fee for hosted accounts to cover storage/IO costs; for enterprise contracts this is often negotiated away or credited against committed spend. We'll reflect that in the rate card line-item as either a $/request or a $/1M cache reads.
- Prefetch/warm generation counts as normal model compute (we treat prefetch like any other generation job), so those tokens are billable at the normal rate unless you want us to run those jobs on a discounted batch/export path (we can propose a separate discounted precompute SKU).

I'll loop Karthik for a confirmation of the exact wording so procurement has clean language for the contract. Also copying Marissa for billing/commit implications.

Would you be open to a short call tomorrow to align on commitment bands and whether we should waive the cache-read fee?

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Priyom — quick technical clarifications to make the answer contract-safe. You can paste this into legal/procurement: 

1) Exact-match cache hit (full response available): Redwood does not execute the forward/backward pass for the cached segment. No model compute tokens are billed for the cached segment. Only the following are billable: any token generation after the cached segment, and a negotiated cache-read fee (if applicable).

2) Partial-match (prefix covered but model must extend/adjust): We bill for the compute required to complete the request — that will include the portion that the model needs to reprocess. In practice partial hits often require re-embedding or KV cache reconstruction; treat them as normal requests for billing purposes.

3) Cache TTL and eviction: cached entries have a TTL by default (30 days) and are subject to eviction for space. If Acme wants pinned residency for certain entries (longer TTL / guaranteed residency), we can offer a residency add-on that carries a per-entry storage/replication fee. That will be a separate line on the invoice.

4) Prefetch: any proactive generation (you ask Redwood to precompute responses) is billed fully at generation rates. We can offer a bulk precompute discount if you run scheduled batches (example: nightly precompute for top-10k prefixes).

5) Metering: we'll expose a per-request metric in Console that breaks out: cache_hit(true|false), cached_bytes, cached_entry_id, cache_read_fee_incurred. That should make it trivial for you to map the invoice to traffic.

Marissa — recommend we propose a short-term concession: waive cache-read fee for first 3 months post-go-live on an initial 12-month commit >= $150k/month. Thoughts?

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice —

Looping back with specifics from Engineering + Billing below (summary):

- Exact cache hit: model compute for cached span = $0; billed only for any subsequent new tokens.
- Partial hit/fallback: full request billed as normal.
- Cache retrieval fee: nominal $0.50 per 10k reads on standard hosted plans; for Enterprise we can waive for the first 90 days given a 12-month $150k+/month commit.
- Prefetch: billable as generation unless run through batch precompute SKU (60% rate) — we can include that SKU in your contract.
- Visibility: we'll add cache-level telemetry to your Console workspace (cache_hit, cached_entry_id, cached_bytes) to make reconciliation trivial.

Next steps: 1) If that aligns, I'll update the rate card and send a redline. 2) Optional: 30-minute call today to walk through the spreadsheet and show a sample cost model in Console. What time works?
